title: Residential Property Condition Disclosure Statement
description: South Carolina Code §27-50-40 requires sellers of residential real property to provide a completed Residential Property Condition Disclosure Statement to the buyer. The disclosure covers known defects in structural, mechanical, plumbing, electrical, and environmental systems. Sellers must disclose conditions they are aware of; the standard is actual knowledge, not constructive knowledge.

required_actions.note: Must be delivered to buyer before or at the time the buyer makes an offer. Buyer has right to rescind within 3 days of receipt.

title: Attorney-Close State Requirement
description: South Carolina is an attorney-close state. The South Carolina Supreme Court has held that the preparation of legal instruments related to real estate transactions constitutes the practice of law. A licensed South Carolina attorney must supervise or conduct closings, prepare deeds, and certify title. SC Ethics Advisory Opinion 94-27 and case law (State v. Buyers Service Co.) reinforce this requirement.

required_actions.note: A South Carolina licensed attorney must supervise the closing, prepare the deed, and certify title.

citations: State v. Buyers Service Co., 292 S.C. 426 (1987)
S.C. Code Ann. §40-5-310 (unauthorized practice of law)

title: Brokerage Relationship Disclosure
description: South Carolina requires licensees to disclose their brokerage relationships at the first practical opportunity. Dual agency is permitted only with written informed consent of both parties. The SC Real Estate Commission requires use of the approved agency disclosure form.

required_actions.note: Must be presented at first practical opportunity, prior to any substantive discussions about specific property.

title: Coastal Zone and Tidelands Disclosure
description: For properties in the coastal zone, South Carolina requires disclosure of any OCRM (Office of Ocean and Coastal Resource Management) permits, setback lines, and critical area designations. Sellers must disclose if property is seaward of the OCRM baseline or affected by beach renourishment.

required_actions.note: Disclose OCRM baseline position, setback requirements, and any critical area permits.

citations: S.C. Code Ann. §48-39-10 et seq. (Beachfront Management Act)

title: Lead-Based Paint Disclosure (Pre-1978)
description: Federal law requires disclosure of known lead-based paint hazards for residential properties built before 1978. Sellers must provide buyers with an EPA-approved information pamphlet and allow a 10-day lead inspection period.
